calls.head: Active D vs. forward-led
calls.body: The Avalanche’s defensemen shoot a lot, and the Wild’s not so much. Colorado is one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and Minnesota is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Avalanche’s defensemen jump into the play.

calls.head: In close vs. from distance
calls.body: The Wild get in close, but the Avalanche mostly shoot from distance. Minnesota is near the top of the league for shots from in close, and Colorado is the worst. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Wild to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Hughes forces a shootout with a minute left, and the Avalanche win it
paras: What a comeback. Joel Eriksson Ek and Blake Coleman scored less than five minutes apart in the first to put the Wild up 2-0. Eriksson Ek scored again with 44 seconds left in the second to make it 3-0. With the goalie pulled and less than seven minutes left, Devon Toews got the Avalanche on the board. With the goalie still pulled and just under four minutes left, Artturi Lehkonen cut Minnesota’s lead to 3-2. With the goalie still pulled and a minute left, T.J. Hughes tied it 3-3. Cale Makar scored the only goal of the shootout for the Avs.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. The Wild hit two posts and still lost. Mackenzie Blackwood made 19 saves for the Avalanche, and Jesper Wallstedt stopped 28 of 31 at the other end. The Avalanche improved to 15-7-3 and climbed to second in the Central, while the Wild fell to 18-4-6, still first in the NHL in points.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Avalanche.
Kirill Kaprizov’s eight-game point streak against Colorado ended.
Blake Coleman has scored in three straight games.
The Wild’s Nick Foligno played his 1,300th NHL game.
